content.title: Ordinance No. 4917
content.summary: Ordinance No. 4917 amends the Land Development Code of Arvada to regulate short-term rentals (STRs) more effectively, aiming to balance the economic benefits of STRs with the preservation of neighborhood character and the availability of long-term rental housing. The ordinance establishes health and safety requirements for STRs, provides clear permitting guidelines, and ensures that STR owners contribute taxes similar to other lodging facilities. The City Council's goal is to create a sustainable STR program that addresses community concerns while supporting property owners.
content.body:
**COUNCIL BILL NO. 26-001**

ORDINANCE NO. 4917 

AN ORDINANCE REPEALING AND REENACTING OR AMENDING VARIOUS SECTIONS OF THE LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE OF THE ARVADA CITY CODE RELATING TO SHORT-TERM RENTALS 

WHEREAS, the City has the power and authority as a home rule city under Article XX of the Colorado Constitution, and under article 20 of Title 29 and article 23 of Title 31 of the Colorado Revised Statutes to zone and otherwise regulate land within its boundaries; and 

WHEREAS, the City has for many years regulated the business use of residential properties and currently regulates short-term rental (STR) properties; and 

WHEREAS, the City Council wishes to take reasonable steps to prevent the loss of rental housing stock and otherwise support affordable housing efforts in Arvada; and 

WHEREAS, Arvada wishes to more fully integrate STR units into existing neighborhoods while preserving the residential character of these neighborhoods by addressing the potential adverse impacts of STRs including increased noise and traffic; and  

WHEREAS, the City Council finds it necessary to put into place minimum health and safety requirements to protect STR occupants  as well as to protect the health, safety, and welfare of residents; and 

WHEREAS, the City wishes to provide prospective and current STR permittees with clear guidance about permitting requirements and how to lawfully operate an STR in Arvada to support their desire for economic gain; and 

WHEREAS, understanding that STRs are a business use of residential properties, the City wishes to ensure that STR owners pay taxes like other transient lodging facilities including hotels, motels, inns, and bed and breakfast facilities; and 

WHEREAS, the City Council wishes to balance the needs and rights of neighbors and property owners and otherwise create a more sustainable STR Program; and 

WHEREAS, by repealing and reenacting a more robust STR ordinance and creating an STR P be more closely aligned with these findings and goals. 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ARVADA, COLORADO: 

Section 1.  Section 3-1-5-3, Short Term Rentals, of Division 3-1-5, Business Use of the Home, of Article 3-1, Primary Land Use Regulations, of Chapter 3, Use Regulations, of Part III, Land Development Code, of the Arvada City Code is hereby retitled, repealed, and reenacted to read as follows:

## 3-1-5-3. Short-term rentals.

A.              Short title. This section of the Land Development Code (LDC) may be known as the Short-term Rental or STR ordinance.

B.              Legislative declaration and purpose. The purpose of this section is to authorize the operation and regulation of Short-term Rentals (STRs) as a land use within Arvada. The City Council finds that STRs support a vibrant economy and provide real property owners with significant financial benefits. They influence property values and impact neighborhood character by allowing the business use of dwellings in residential neighborhoods. They also reduce the potential availability of long-term rental housing to support the local economy and community.

The City Council also finds that STRs require services and infrastructure to operate. They require regulation as a distinct land use to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of the community through the application of zoning police powers. This section supports the operation of STRs by balancing the need to preserve neighborhood quality of life with the protection of private property rights. The City Council finds that this ordinance and the establishment of STR Program Rules are necessary to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the public.

This section is intended to ensure the health and safety of STR Occupants while preserving neighborhood character by mitigating the negative impacts of STRs on the neighborhoods where they are located. This section is also intended to ensure that STR operations are conducted lawfully, and that the activities of Marketplace Facilitators are appropriately regulated. Finally, this section is intended to ensure that the City utilizes this and other applicable provisions in the City Code including the LDC to enforce the provisions of this section as appropriate through the exercise of civil and criminal remedies.

C.              Authority. The authority to establish and implement an STR Program is set forth in section 1-1-1-3 of this LDC.

D.              Applicability. This section applies to any Property located in Arvada that is being offered for Rent as or being used as an STR whether or not it is permitted. STR licenses that are valid at the time this ordinance goes into effect will remain in effect until the date they expire, or are suspended, revoked, or abandoned, whichever occurs first. Nothing in this section precludes the rental of a Dwelling for 30 or more consecutive days.

E.               Definitions. Certain terms used in this STR ordinance are defined in section 11-3-3-1 of the Land Development Code.

F.               Duties and responsibilities of the Director. The Director shall implement, administer, and enforce this section of the LDC and the STR Program Rules (Rules) as set forth in section 8-1-1-1 of this LDC.

G.              Permit and business license required.

1.               STR permit. Each Property being offered for Rent, rented, or being used as an STR must have an STR Permit as required under this section 3-1-5-3. A Permit may be for either a primary or a non-primary residence.

2.               Business license. A Permittee holding an STR Permit must also hold a valid city-issued business license while the STR Permit is in effect. A business license application will be processed and a business license may be issued by the director of finance as set forth in the City Code.

H.              Permit requirements  generally. An STR Permittee must comply with all the requirements of this section 3-1-5-3. In addition, the following requirements must be met to hold and maintain an STR Permit:

1.               Natural person. Except as otherwise noted in this section 3-1-5-3 or in the Rules, a Permit may only be issued in the name of one natural person 18 years of age or older who has an Ownership Interest of 20 percent or more in the Property for which the Permit is issued or who is the named beneficiary of a trust holding the Property to be permitted.

a.                Permits or licenses issued to entities. An entity that holds a Permit or license on May 1, 2026, may continue to hold that Permit for the duration of its term. Should an entity apply to renew a Permit, the entity must designate a natural person to be its Permitee. Should a Permit held by an entity lapse, expire, be abandoned, or be revoked, or should the Property be sold or otherwise transferred, a new Permit issued for that Property must be issued in the name of a natural person.

2.               Limit. No person may hold more than three STR Permits at a time.

3.               Number. Each Permit will be assigned a unique number. The Permit number must be clearly displayed in all advertising and listings of the STR, including but not limited to all digital and print advertising.

4.                  Term. Each Permit is valid for one year from the date of issuance. As an example, a Permit issued on March 20 of a year will be valid through March 19 of the following year unless it is suspended, revoked, or abandoned. Each Permit may be renewed annually according to the provisions set forth in this section 3-1-5-3 and in the Rules.

5.               Non-transferable. A Permit will be issued solely to the Permittee to whom it is issued and only for the Property for which it is issued. A Permit does not run with the Property but is issued to a specific person. A Permit is not transferable or assignable to any other person, entity, address, or location.

a.                Effect of sale or transfer of property rights. If at any time during the term of a Permit, the Permittee sells or otherwise transfers their Ownership Interest in the Property, or if the Permittee's Ownership Interest in the Property falls below 20 percent, the Permit will be deemed terminated and revoked as of the date of the sale or transfer.

6.               Contingent upon compliance. Each Permit is contingent on compliance with this section 3-1-5-3, with any conditions placed on the Permit by the Director, with the provisions of the Rules, with the city's property maintenance, fire, and other building codes, with the provisions of this LDC, and all other applicable municipal and State laws.

7.               Taxes paid. The Permittee must ensure that all Lodging, sales, and other taxes due as a result of the use of the Property as STR are submitted to the city in a timely manner.

I.                Permit applications  generally; actions by the Director. STR Permit Applications must be submitted in accordance with this section 3-1-5-3 and the Rules.

1.               Application not accepted. The Director may not accept an incomplete Application. The Director may not accept an Application for a Permit from a person or entity that has, within one year prior to the date of the Application, had any Arvada STR Permit revoked, or who has been found guilty in the municipal court of operating an STR without a Permit, of not posting an STR Permit inside a Property being offered for Rent, rented, or used as an STR, of falsifying, defacing, or altering an STR Permit, of not having a business license while offering an STR for Rent, Renting, or using a Property as an STR, or of non-payment of Lodging, sales, and other taxes as required under this section 3-1-5-3 and Chapter 98 of the City Code.

2.               Actions by the Director. The Director may issue a Permit, issue it with conditions, or deny it. The Director may issue a permit electronically or may require that a Permit or renewal Permit be issued to the Permittee in person.

J.                Emergency contact. A Permittee must designate an emergency contact (EC) whose responsibilities are set forth in the Rules.

K.              Inspections. By filing an Application, the Applicant is deemed to have consented to inspections of the Property to determine eligibility for a Permit, or for the purpose of determining compliance with all other applicable laws. Inspections may be made as a part of the initial or renewal permitting process and will be made upon reasonable notice. The Director may, at their sole discretion, allow any inspection required or necessitated under this section 3-1-5-3 to be conducted by a city inspector or by a third party licensed or certified inspector. Nothing in this section may be deemed to affect the ability of a Peace Officer or other first responder to respond to a call for service or other incident at a Property being offered for Rent, rented, or being used as an STR.

L.               Operating requirements. A Permittee must comply with the following operating requirements:

1.               Parking requirement. Any property being offered for Rent, rented, or used as an STR must have one additional on-site parking space.

Exception. If the entire premises are being used or rented as an STR, no additional on-site parking space is required.

2.               Property maintenance requirements. The Permittee must maintain weekly rubbish and garbage removal services for the STR and otherwise comply with all provisions of the International Property Maintenance Code (IPMC) as adopted by Arvada. This includes but is not limited to complying with lawn mowing, weed removal, and snow and ice removal requirements.

3.               Nuisances not allowed. A Permittee may not allow or permit the STR to create a nuisance as that term is defined in Chapter 38 of the City Code.

4.               Limits on overnight occupancy. STRs are limited to a total overnight Occupancy of two Occupants per bedroom plus two additional Occupants; studios are limited to a total overnight Occupancy of three Occupants. Each Permit Application must list the number of bedrooms in the STR unit at its largest configuration. The maximum number of overnight Occupants for an STR must be included in all advertising for that STR.

5.               Property to be rented. A Permittee may rent the entire permitted Property or a bedroom, lock-off, or other portion of the permitted Property.

6.               Maximum nights in operation. No STR may be occupied by Guests or Occupants for more than any 240 days in any 365-day period. 

M.             Building and zoning restrictions generally.

1.               Permitted buildings. An STR may be allowed in a primary Dwelling. A Dwelling designated as affordable housing or that is otherwise deed-restricted may not be used as an STR.

2.               Number of STRs per lot. Only one STR Permit may be issued per Lot. 

N.               Records.

1.               Permittee. Each Permittee must maintain the following records from the date their Permit was issued. If the Permit is a renewal permit, the Permittee must also maintain these records for one year before the current permit was issued:

a.               Total number of nights the STR was rented to a Guest;

b.               The dates on which the STR was rented to a Guest; and

c.               Other records necessary to comply with the provisions of this section 3-1-5-3.

2.               Marketplace facilitator. Each Marketplace Facilitator must maintain the following information for STR transactions for each Property being offered for Rent on or through their platform in Arvada for five years from the date of the transaction:

a.               The name of the Permittee who offered the STR for Rent;

b.               The address of the STR;

c.               The dates on which the STR was booked by a Guest;

d.               The price paid by the Guest for each STR transaction; and

e.               The STR Permit number.

O.              Fees. Each Applicant may be charged an Application fee, an annual Permit or renewal Permit fee, and other fees as noted in the applicable fees schedule.

P.               Lodging, sales, and other tax payments required. A Permittee must obtain and maintain a City of Arvada business license in addition to an STR Permit and must remit Lodging, sales, and other taxes in accordance with article V of Chapter 98 of the Arvada City Code.

1.               Financial audits. To ensure ongoing eligibility for an STR Permit, Permittees are subject to audits by the City's finance department as set forth in article V of Chapter 98 of the Arvada City Code.

Q.              Enforcement. Arvada actively enforces this section and STR Program Rules through inspections, responding to complaints, audits, and permitting activities. Enforcement activities play a vital role in assisting Occupants in supporting neighborhood values and Permittees in complying with applicable laws and the Rules. This section 3-1-5-3 may be enforced by the Director and by those employees designated as Peace Officers under section 58-2 of the Arvada City Code. By applying for an STR Permit, the Applicant is deemed to have acknowledged and to understand that both criminal penalties and administrative consequences may flow from the same act or failure to act. Enforcement mechanisms and appeal rights are as set forth in this section and in the Rules.

1.               No warning required. Notwithstanding any other provision of the LDC, and understanding the crucial role enforcement plays in public safety and in maintaining the peaceful enjoyment of the city's neighborhoods, a Peace Officer is not required to issue a warning or similar notice of violation, or a stop work order before issuing a summons and complaint for any of the following violations:

a.          Not having an STR Permit;

b.          Not posting the STR Permit inside the Property;

c.          Falsifying, defacing, or altering an STR Permit;

d.          Not having a business license when offering an STR for Rent, renting, or while using a Property as an STR;

e.          Exceeding overnight Occupancy limits under the STR's Permit;

f.          Allowing or permitting a Large Social Gathering at a Property while it is being rented or used as an STR;

g.          Not having a functioning smoke detector, carbon monoxide detector, or fire extinguisher in or upon the permitted premises;

h.          Not obtaining a building or other permit required under Chapter 18 of the Arvada City Code before beginning the work for which the building permit is required;

i.           Unlawfully removing a Red Tag placard;

j.           Unlawfully entering or occupying a property that has been posted with a Red Tag placard; or

k.          Non-payment of Lodging, sales, and other taxes as required under this section 3-1-5-3 and Chapter 98 of the City Code.

R.              Unlawful acts  generally. It shall be unlawful for a Permittee to fail to comply with any requirement or provision of or to engage in any act that is declared to be unlawful under this section 3-1-5-3.

1.     Advertising. It shall be unlawful for any person or Marketplace Facilitator to knowingly advertise or list an STR without the STR Permit number clearly displayed on the face of the advertisement or listing. In this subsection, the term "advertise" means the act of drawing the public's attention to a Property for the purpose of offering the Property for Rent as or for using it as an STR. The advertisement may be made by or through any platform or medium.

2.               Unlawful to rent or use unpermitted property as an STR. It shall be unlawful for any person, whether a principal or agent, clerk, or employee, either for themself, or for any other person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use Property as an STR without first obtaining an STR Permit.

3.               Unlawful transactions. It shall be unlawful for any person or Marketplace Facilitator to knowingly advertise or facilitate the rental or use of an unpermitted STR, or to receive payment, directly or indirectly, for renting or allowing the use of an unpermitted STR located in the city.

4.               Minimum rental period. It shall be unlawful for any person or Marketplace Facilitator to knowingly offer a Property for Rent, Rent, or use a Property as an STR for fewer than two consecutive days.

5.               Permit displayed. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use a Property as an STR without affixing a valid STR Permit near the primary entrance to the STR in such a way as to be clearly visible to an ordinarily observant person entering the STR.

6.               Unlawful to alter permit. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly falsify, deface, or alter an STR Permit.

7.               Video recording devices prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use as an STR Property that contains or is equipped with a device that records moving or still images of the inside of the Property. A video recording device that captures only images of outdoor locations upon Property used as an STR, such as a porch, driveway, lawn, garden, patio, or deck is allowed.

a.                This subsection does not prohibit a Guest or Occupant from using a video recording device to record images of the inside of the Property if the recording is made in or from an area they are otherwise allowed to be in, and if the recording is otherwise legal.

b.               This subsection does not prohibit a Peace Officer, fire official, emergency medical responder, city inspector, or other city official from using a video recording device to record images of the inside of the Property while acting within the course and scope of their employment.

C.    This subsection does not prohibit a Permittee or Permittee's agent from using a video recording device to record images of the inside of the Permitted Property if each Guest or Occupant on or within the Property at the time of the recording has been notified of and has consented to the recording before it occurs, or prohibit a Permittee or Permittee's agent from using a video recording device to record images of the inside of the Property when no one is renting it.

8.               Marketplace facilitator  business license. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly broker or facilitate an STR reservation online and receive payment for this service without first obtaining a business license from the city.

9.               Marketplace facilitator  removal of listing. It shall be unlawful for any person or Marketplace Facilitator to knowingly fail to remove an unpermitted STR from the person's or Marketplace Facilitator's website or other digital platform within 7 calendar days of receiving notification from the Director that the STR is not permitted or that the Permit has been suspended or revoked.

10.            Records. It shall be unlawful for any person offering a Property for Rent, renting, or using a Property as an STR to knowingly fail to keep or maintain STR records as required under this section 3-1-5-3.

S.                  Unlawful acts  business operations.

1.               False statement of fact. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly make a false statement of a material fact on an STR Permit Application or renewal Permit Application or in any document accompanying an Application.

2.               Safety requirements. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use Property as an STR if the Property is not equipped with a functioning smoke detector, carbon monoxide detector, and fire extinguisher.

3.               Unlawful to remove red tag placard. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly deface or alter a Red Tag placard, or for any person to knowingly remove a Red Tag placard except at the direction of the Director or the chief building official or designee thereof.

4.               Unlawful to enter red tagged property. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly enter or occupy any Property, structure, or portion of any Property or structure upon which a Red Tag placard has been posted except for the purpose of repairing or otherwise bringing the Property into compliance with this section 3-1-5-3 or into compliance with any other provision of the City Code, including but not limited to the city's  property maintenance, fire, and other building codes.

5.               Compliance with city and state laws. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use a Property that does not comply with all applicable city and state laws as an STR.

6.               Insurance. It shall be unlawful to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use Property as an STR without fire, hazard, and liability insurance within the coverage limits set by the Director.

7.               Business license required. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use Property as an STR without first having obtained a city-issued business license.

8.               Taxation. It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly Rent, offer for Rent, or use Property as an STR to fail to pay Lodging, sales, and other taxes owed to the City as required under Chapter 98 of this Code.

T.               Unlawful acts  good neighbor provisions.

1.               Exceeding overnight occupancy. It shall be unlawful for any person including but not limited to a Guest or Occupant to knowingly allow or permit more people to occupy an STR than are allowed as set forth on the STR's Permit.

2.               Unreasonable noise prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person including a Guest of or Occupant at or upon a Property being rented or used as an STR to knowingly make, allow, or permit unreasonable Noise from or upon the Property or Noise that is otherwise in violation of any provision of Chapter 38 of this Code.

3.               Rubbish and garbage. It shall be unlawful for any person, including but not limited to the Permittee, Guest of, or Occupant at or upon a Property being rented or used as an STR to knowingly fail to dispose of rubbish and garbage at the STR no less often than once per week.

4.               Snow and ice removal. It shall be unlawful for any person, including but not limited to the Permittee, Guest of, or Occupant at or upon a Property being rented or used as an STR to knowingly fail to remove snow and ice from the Property within 24 hours of the end of any snow fall or ice storm as set forth in the International Property Maintenance Code as adopted by the City.

5.               Large social gatherings prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person, including but not limited to the Permittee, Guest of, or Occupant at or upon a Property being rented or used as an STR to knowingly allow or permit a Large Social Gathering on the Property while the Property is being rented as or used as an STR.

6.               Failure to physically report upon request. It shall be unlawful for the Permittee to knowingly fail to physically report to the STR for which they hold a Permit within one hour of being asked to do so by a Peace Officer, or, if the Permittee if unavailable, for the designated EC to fail to physically report to the STR within one hour of being asked to do so by a Peace Officer.

U.              Criminal penalties; other remedies; concurrent remedies.

1.               Criminal penalty. Except as otherwise noted herein, a violation of this section shall be punished by a fine or imprisonment not to exceed the limits established in section 1-5 of the City Code, except that the penalty for any violation under this section for which there is a counterpart in Chapter 62 or elsewhere in the City Code will be the same as the penalty for the counterpart violation.

2.               Determination of guilt. Guilt may be found as a result of a no contest plea, a plea of guilty, or by conviction in the municipal court.

3.               Minimum fines. A person who is found guilty in the municipal court of offering an unpermitted Property for Rent as an STR, of renting, or of using an unpermitted Property as an STR, of not posting the STR Permit inside the Property, or of falsifying, defacing, or altering an STR Permit shall be fined a minimum of $2000.00 per violation. A person guilty of a violation of any other provision of this section 3-1-5-3 shall be fined according to the following minimum fine schedule:

a.                  First conviction. Minimum fine of $500.00 per violation.

b.                  Second conviction within any 365-day period. Minimum fine of $1000.00 per violation.

c.                  Third or subsequent conviction within any 365-day period. Minimum fine of $2000.00 per violation.

The operative date for calculating the date of the second or third conviction is the date of the violation for which the person is convicted or pleads guilty or no contest, not the date of the conviction or plea. No portion of these minimum fines may be suspended. A municipal court judge may impose conditions in connection with the minimum penalties set forth herein and may impose a greater sentence including imprisonment based on the facts and circumstances of the case and in accordance with section 1-5 of the City Code.

4.               Continuing violation. In accordance with section 1-5 of the City Code, every day any violation of this section continues or is permitted or allowed to continue shall constitute a separate violation.

V.                Other administrative and civil remedies. The Director may institute administrative proceedings against a Permittee, including but not limited to a Permittee who has been found guilty of a violation of this section 3-1-5-3, as set forth in the Rules. In addition, the city attorney may institute injunctive, abatement, or other appropriate action to prevent, restrain, enjoin, correct, abate, or remove a violation of this section 3-1-5-3 or any other section of the Code when it occurs.

W.               Concurrent remedies. The initiation of a prosecution in the municipal court for a violation of this section shall not preclude the city from instituting administrative proceedings against a Permittee or from taking other appropriate action to restrain, enjoin, correct, or abate, or remove a violation, or to stop an illegal act or conduct. Enforcement of the provisions of this ordinance may be conducted by a Peace Officer as a criminal matter, by the Director as an administrative matter, and by other city officials as appropriate.

X.                Liens. Until paid, any delinquent charges, assessments, or taxes made or levied by the City pursuant to this section against a Property being offered for Rent as or used as an STR shall, as of recording, be a lien against the property on which the violation has been found to exist. If not paid within 30 calendar days from the date of the statement, the city clerk may certify any unpaid charges, assessments, or taxes to the county treasurer to be collected and paid over by the county treasurer in the same manner as taxes are authorized to be by statute together with a ten percent penalty for costs of collection. Any lien placed against the property pursuant to this section will be recorded with the county clerk and recorder."

**Section 2.**Subsection 8-1-1-1B.1, Duties and Responsibilities, of section 8-1-1-1, Director of community and economic development, of Division 8-1-1, City Staff and Referral Agencies, of Article 8-1, Development Review Bodies, of Chapter 8, Development Review Process, of Part III, Land Development Code, of the Arvada City Code is hereby amended by adding a new subsection g to subsection B.1 to read as follows:

"B Duties and Responsibilities. The Director shall be responsible for the administration of this LDC and the regulations contained therein.

1.    The Director shall have the authority to:

. . . .

g.               Implement, administer, and enforce the STR ordinance and Program Rules and in relation thereto, may:

i.                 Require access to each Property being used or operated as an STR or for which an STR Permit is sought to conduct a pre-permitting, renewal or compliance inspection, and to implement, administer, and enforce section 3-1-5-3 of this LDC and STR Program Rules. The Director may require minimum insurance coverage for STRs in types and amounts to be determined in consultation with the city's insurance and risk program director;

ii.               Cause a Red Tag placard to be posted on an unpermitted Property or structure when the Director has good cause to believe it is being offered for Rent, rented, or being used as an STR, or on any permitted STR that has been or is being operated in a manner that adversely affects the health, safety, or welfare of any occupant or the neighborhood in which it is located or that has been or is being operated in violation of any provision set forth in this section 3-1-5-3;

iii.             Issue orders to show cause and notices to appear, make compliance determinations, and impose administrative consequences on Permittees including but not limited to suspending or revoking a permit;

iv.             Ensure that Marketplace Facilitators offer only permitted properties for Rent as STRs by requiring a Marketplace Facilitator to remove an advertisement or listing for an STR from the Marketplace Facilitator's website or other digital platform if the STR Permit for the Property has been suspended or revoked or otherwise as appropriate;

v.               Maintain and make publicly available a registry of all permitted STRs within the city; and

vi.             Take or delegate any other action reasonably necessary to implement, administer, and enforce the STR ordinance. Nothing in this section affects the ability of a Peace Officer to investigate suspected offenses involving STRs and initiate prosecutions of cases involving STRs."

The remaining portions of subsection 8-1-1-1B.1 shall remain unchanged.

**Section 3.**Section 11-3-3-1, Definitions, of Division 11-3-3, Definitions, of Article 11-3 Definitions, of Chapter 11, Measurements, Rules of Construction, and Definitions, of Part III, Land Development Code, of the Arvada City Code is hereby amended by repealing and reenacting or adding certain definitions to read as follows:

"Applicant. Unless otherwise specified, an owner or other person with a legal property interest, application for subdivision or development. Applicant also includes a natural person with an ownership interest in
